title: Sharded Matrix Multiplication
prompt:
Implement column-sharded matrix multiplication and its backward pass with NumPy. Let `a` have shape `(batch, in_features)`. `b_shards` is a non-empty list where shard `i` has shape `(in_features, out_i)`; concatenating the shards along axis 1 gives the logical weight matrix `B`. Inputs must be two-dimensional numeric arrays with consistent dimensions. Do not mutate them.

### Part 1 — Distributed forward pass

Implement `column_sharded_matmul(a, b_shards)`. Compute `a @ shard` independently for every shard and concatenate the partial outputs along axis 1. Return a NumPy array equal to `a @ np.concatenate(b_shards, axis=1)`.

### Part 2 — Backpropagation across shards

Implement `column_sharded_matmul_with_grads(a, b_shards, dy)`, where `dy` has the same shape as the logical output. Return `(y, da, db_shards)`. Split `dy` by shard output width. Each shard computes its local output, input-gradient contribution, and weight gradient. `da` is the sum of all input-gradient contributions, modeling an all-reduce; `db_shards[i]` remains local to shard `i`. Preserve floating-point precision and validate malformed shapes with `ValueError`.

example.reasoning: Each device computes its output columns locally, then the results are concatenated.
